metadata.title: The Effect of Inquiry-Based Practices on Scientific Literacy: the Mediating Role of Science Attitudes

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2015 microdata for eight countries and models a two-level structure (students at level 1, schools at level 2) in Mplus. The authors state that, to achieve higher accuracy, “sampling weight” was considered in the analyses, but they do not report the specific weight variable name(s) used. For descriptive statistics and correlations, they used pairwise deletion, and for the multilevel structural equation mediation analyses they omitted cases with missing values because Mplus could not process them. The paper also codes missing values as “999” for variables used in the study, indicating a preprocessing step prior to modeling.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of PISA 2015 for eight selected countries (China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, USA, Germany, Australia, Finland). Scientific literacy is constructed as the mean of the ten PISA 2015 plausible values for science. Missing values for variables used in the study are coded as “999”; for the multilevel structural equation mediation analyses, cases with missing values are omitted because they cannot be processed in Mplus 8.3, while pairwise deletion is used for descriptive statistics and correlation analyses.

main_findings.performance_metrics: Multilevel structural equation mediation (MSEM) path coefficients by country; model fit: RMSEA 0.036–0.056, CFI 0.909–0.959, TLI 0.899–0.954. Direct effect c (perceived practices → literacy): standardized β = −0.319 to −0.136 across countries. Indirect effects: via interest (a1*b1) positive (0.014–0.085); via self-efficacy (a2*b2) positive (0.014–0.062); via instrumental motivation (a3*b3) negative (−0.024 to −0.006) for six countries (non-significant China and Finland).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2015 Science data from eight countries, the study leveraged perceived inquiry-based practices together with science interest, science self-efficacy, and instrumental motivation (plus ESCS and gender controls) to model scientific literacy (mean of 10 plausible values) in a two-level mediation framework, finding that the direct effect of perceived inquiry-based practices on scientific literacy was consistently negative across countries (β = −0.319 to −0.136) while indirect effects via interest in science and self-efficacy were consistently positive and the indirect effect via instrumental motivation was negative for six of eight countries. This indicates that simply increasing students’ perceived exposure to inquiry activities may not improve science achievement unless it also strengthens adaptive science attitudes (interest and self-efficacy), and that instrumental motivation may require more autonomy-supportive designs to avoid undermining literacy, though the cross-sectional design limits causal interpretation.

data.outcome_summary: This study used PISA 2015 science data for eight countries (China, Japan, Korea, Singapore, USA, Germany, Australia, Finland; total N=60,812 students) to test a two-level mediation model in Mplus (students nested in schools). Scientific literacy was operationalized as the mean of the ten PISA plausible values for science. The model fit was acceptable across countries (RMSEA ≈ 0.036–0.056; CFI ≈ 0.909–0.959; TLI ≈ 0.899–0.954). Results showed a consistently negative direct path from perceived inquiry-based practices to scientific literacy (standardized β from −0.319 to −0.136), but positive indirect effects through interest in science and science self-efficacy, and a negative indirect effect through instrumental motivation for six countries (China and Finland were exceptions). The study also used sampling weights “considered” in analyses and omitted cases with missing values for MSEM, and it interprets associations rather than causal effects due to cross-sectional PISA data.
